answer: Each agent must lock a collateral bond and be vouched by three already-staked peers. Vouches form a graph: an agent earns rewards only if its voucher chain reaches a trusted vertex. A clone stays in a tiny closed reef of accounts vouching only for one another, so it earns nothing. To escape, an attacker funds a fresh bond per fake and bribes genuine outsiders, whose own stake is slashed when an audit finds the cluster. At the nadir of a crackdown every bond is lost at once, so minting thousands of agents costs real capital, not just CPU.
